chunks: O believers, do not hold Jews and Christians as your allies. They are allies of one another; and anyone who makes them his friends is surely one of them; and God does not guide the unjust.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّهُمْ: he makes them his allies / takes charge of them

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about believers taking Jews and Christians as allies?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as establishing a principle of political and spiritual distinctiveness rather than a total prohibition on all interactions, emphasizing loyalty to the Ahl al-Bayt and the faithful. The phrase 'they are allies of one another' highlights the cohesive nature of the People of the Book in contrast to the monotheistic community, warning that close alliance can lead to adopting their theological or political stances. This concept of 'Wala' and 'Bara' (loyalty and disavowal) is central to Shia identity, distinguishing believers from other religious communities in matters of faith and governance.
